data.name: Joshian
data.gender_notes: Joshian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Joshian is a variant of the Hebrew name Joshua, which translates to 'God is salvation' or 'God saves'. In the Hebrew Bible, Joshua is the name of a prophet and a military leader, who led the Israelites to conquer the Promised Land after the death of Moses. The name Joshian carries the meaning “God is salvation” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Joshian usually hope their child will grow to embody god is salvation and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Joshian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God is salvation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Joshian total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: יושיאן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יושיאן הוא צורה משונת של יהושע, שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא המושיע' או 'האל יושיע'. השם נגזר מהמילים העבריות 'ישע' (להושיע) ו'אלוהים' (אלוהים). השם יהושע היה שמו של נושא הנס גדול בישראל, שפילד את עם ישראל למלחמה והושיע אותם מידי האויבים.

in_greek.name: Ιωσίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιωσίας είναι μια ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος יהושע (Yehoshua), που σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός σώζει' ή 'Ο Θεός είναι ο σωτήρας'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα Ιησούς (Iesous) ήταν μια ελληνική μορφή του יהושע, που χρησιμοποιήθηκε για να αναφερθεί στον Ιησού Χριστό.

in_latin.name: Iosias
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Iosias derivatur ex nomine hebraeo יהושע (Yehoshua), quod significat 'Deus salvat' vel 'Deus est salvator'. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Iesus (Iosus) erat forma latina nominis יהושע, quod usurpabatur ad designandum Iesum Christum.

in_english.name: Joshian
in_english.meaning: God saves or God is salvation
in_english.long_meaning: The name Joshian is a variant of the Hebrew name יהושע (Yehoshua), which means 'God saves' or 'God is salvation'. The name is derived from the Hebrew words 'yasha' (to save) and 'El' (God). In the Bible, Joshua was a prominent figure who led the Israelites to victory and saved them from their enemies. The name has been adopted in various Christian traditions, symbolizing spiritual salvation and divine protection.

data.cultural_impact: The name Joshian can signify strength, courage, and leadership, inspired by the biblical figure of Joshua. In Christian households, the name may be associated with faith, resilience, and the promise of a better future.
data.spiritual_significance: Joshian holds a deep spiritual meaning rooted in the idea of salvation and divine providence. It reminds Christians that God is with them in their struggles and challenges, and that He provides them with the strength and resources to overcome adversities. The name is a constant reminder of God's presence and faithfulness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Joshian: God is our salvation. This name, derived from Joshua in the Old Testament, symbolizes trust and reliance in God's deliverance and guidance. In spirituality, it represents one's steadfast journey towards a fulfilling life guided by divine providence.

biblical_reference.note: The name Joshua (יהושע) appears frequently in the Hebrew Bible, referring to the leader of the Israelites who conquered Canaan.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Joshian was a 5th century Armenian king. The name Joshian carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Joshian continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.
